newsitem.title: CHINA: First China navy patrol boat casts off to HK.
newsitem.headline: First China navy patrol boat casts off to HK.

text.p: A Chinese navy patrol boat cast off from a wharf near the border town of Shenzhen in the early hours of Tuesday and headed toward Hong Kong to take up the defence of the region on its first day of Beijing rule.
Chinese state television showed the boat, sailors lining the deck, pulling away from the dock after a farewell ceremony of dragon and lion dances.

The vessel, one of 10 set to sail into Hong Kong on Tuesday, was expected to enter the waters of China's new Special Adminstrative Region about 6 a.m. (2200 GMT Monday), an unidentified ship's officer told state television.
The boat was expected to dock in Hong Kong about 8 a.m., the officer said, adding that the vessel had about 200 sailors aboard.
Some 4,000 troops of the People's Liberation Army, navy and air force were due to stream into Hong Kong early on Tuesday, in 10 ships, six helicopters, 21 armoured cars and 400 other vehicles.
